title_orig: Του γεγονότος διερμηνευτού της Οθωμανικής Αυλής η μετά του σοφού οθωμανού Βάνη-Εφέντου, διδασκάλου και ιεροκήρυκος του σουλτάνου Μεχμέτου του Δ', τεθρυλλημένη διάλεξις περί της χριστιανικής πίστεως (Διάλεξις)
title_es: Diálogo de Panagiotis Nikousios con Vani Mehmed Efendi (1662)
title_en: Debate of Panagiotes Nikousios, Grand Dragoman, with Vani Mehmed Efendi, on the Christian faith (1662 debate; manuscript text published 1868)
date: Debate: July 1662 (c. 1662); manuscripts 18th c.; printed 1868 (Pandora vol. 18, issue 427, 1 Jan 1868, pp. 361–371)
genre: Dialogue / record of public debate (anonymous redaction, with a eulogy of Nikousios in some MSS)
edition_original: Ed. I. Sakellion, Πανδώρα τ. ΙΗ', φύλλ. 427 (1 Ian 1868), pp. 361–371 (ed. after MS Patmos 371, ff. 221r–240r, 18th c.). Also Sakellion 1889 (MS Athens; Athens, pp. 235–273 per Kermeli 2017).
edition_english: None read. Public-domain English: none found. (Modern translation by Tzedopoulos in Christian-Muslim Relations vol. 2, Bloomsbury 2018/2023: IN COPYRIGHT, not quoted.)
licence: Pandora (1850–1872) is a 19th-century Greek periodical; the article is public domain. Pleias (Univ. of Patras) hosts it; page images read by me (no OCR text layer).
authenticity_note: Authorship disputed: Kermeli (Bilig 82, 2017) says the debate was recorded by Nikousios himself or by a person in his circle; the text was composed in vernacular Greek, dated 1662–1680. Sakellion's 1868 text is based on MS Patmos (the title does not name Vani). The Muslim speaker's statements are quoted in the Christian record and are not Nikousios's own doctrinal statements.
notes: Printed also as a French summary in Sieur de La Croix, Etat présent des nations et églises grecque, arménienne et maronite en Turquie (1695; 1715 ed. pp. 247–260) — French, not checked page by page. The Patmos MS is bound with a Greek version of Cantacuzenus's Apology; Pandora footnote (a) lists Cantacuzenus's 'Against the Muslim (Mohammed)' oration. Sakellion's text is the only PD Greek printing I could open.
